data.heading: G'day, I'm Liam.
data.body:
I started Spark Life because I kept hearing the same story. Someone books a sparky, takes a day off work, and nobody turns up. Or they turn up, do the job, and leave a pile of plaster dust in the hallway and a bill nobody mentioned beforehand.

None of that is hard to fix. Text people when you're on the way. Quote the job before you start it. Put drop sheets down. Take your mess with you. That's most of the business plan, honestly.

When you book Spark Life you get me, a fully licensed electrician (REC 27391), not a dispatch line and whoever happened to be free. I'll tell you honestly when something can wait, and just as honestly when it can't.

data.heading: The boring but important bit.
data.content:
Spark Life Electrical Contractors is a Registered Electrical Contractor in Victoria, REC 27391, carrying full public liability insurance.

Every job we complete is wired to the AS/NZS 3000 wiring rules and issued with a Certificate of Electrical Safety. You get a copy and so does the electrical safety regulator. It's the document that proves the work in your home was done properly, and it's the one thing an insurer will ask for if you ever need to claim.

If an electrician can't produce a REC number and a certificate, that should end the conversation.

data.heading: Whole home LED changeover.

Thirty-two halogen downlights swapped for dimmable LEDs across two storeys, warm white through the living areas and a cooler neutral in the kitchen and laundry.

We replaced four old leading-edge dimmers at the same time, which is usually the real reason people think LEDs flicker.

data.heading: EV charger, load managed.

A 7kW wall charger into a garage on a board that was already close to full. Rather than a full upgrade we fitted load management, so the charger eases off when the oven and the ducted heating are both running.

Cable run concealed the length of the garage, app configured for off-peak charging, done in a day.

pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.excerpt: How Spark Life Electrical Contractors collects, uses and protects your personal information.

seo.title: Privacy Policy | Spark Life Electrical
seo.desc: How Spark Life Electrical Contractors collects, uses and protects your personal information.

data.content:
This policy explains what personal information Spark Life Electrical Contractors collects, why we collect it, and what we do with it. It is written to meet our obligations under the Australian Privacy Principles.

What we collect

When you contact us by phone, email or through a form on this site, we collect the details you give us. That means your name, phone number, email address, the address of the job, and whatever you tell us about the work you need done.

Why we collect it

Solely to quote and carry out the work you have asked about, to issue certificates and invoices, and to contact you about that job. We do not sell your information and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.

Who we share it with

Only where it is necessary to do the work. For example, providing your details to a supplier arranging a warranty, or lodging a Certificate of Electrical Safety with the relevant regulator as the law requires.

How long we keep it

Job records and certificates are retained for as long as required by Victorian electrical safety and tax law. Enquiries that do not become jobs are deleted once they are no longer useful.

Cookies and analytics

This site may use cookies and analytics to understand how visitors use it. That data is aggregated and does not identify you personally. You can block cookies in your browser without losing access to any part of the site.

Access, correction and complaints

You can ask us what information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it where we are not legally required to keep it. Email info@spark-life.com.au and we will respond within a reasonable time. If you are not satisfied with our response you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner.

data.title: Questions about your details?

pages.title: Terms of Service
pages.excerpt: The terms that apply to quotes, work and payment from Spark Life Electrical Contractors.

seo.title: Terms of Service | Spark Life Electrical
seo.desc: The terms that apply to quotes, work, warranty and payment from Spark Life Electrical Contractors.

data.content:
These terms apply to quotes issued and work carried out by Spark Life Electrical Contractors (REC 27391) unless we have agreed something different with you in writing.

Quotes

Quotes are fixed for the scope described and valid for 30 days. If we open up a wall or a switchboard and find something materially different from what was quoted, we stop, explain it, and give you a revised price before continuing. You will never receive a variation you did not approve first.

Access and site conditions

We need safe access to the work area, the switchboard, and any roof or subfloor space involved. Where access is blocked or unsafe on the day and we cannot proceed, a call-out charge may apply.

Workmanship warranty

Our workmanship is guaranteed. If something we installed or repaired is not right, tell us and we will return and make it right at no cost. Materials and appliances carry their manufacturer's warranty, which we will help you claim.

What is not covered

Pre-existing faults outside the quoted scope, damage caused by others after we leave, and failure of appliances we did not supply are not covered by our workmanship warranty.

Certificates

A Certificate of Electrical Safety is issued for all prescribed work and provided to you on completion. Keep it, because your insurer may ask for it.

Payment

Payment is due on completion unless other terms have been agreed in writing. Larger jobs may be invoiced in stages, set out in the quote.

Cancellation

Let us know as early as you can. Cancellations with less than 24 hours' notice may attract a fee covering materials already ordered for your job.

Australian Consumer Law

Nothing in these terms excludes, restricts or modifies any guarantee, right or remedy you have under the Australian Consumer Law.

data.title: Switchboard Upgrades
data.lead: Ceramic fuses out, safety switches in, on a board you can actually read.

data.heading: Switchboard Upgrades
data.body:
If your board still has ceramic fuses and fuse wire, it was built for a house with a fridge, a kettle and a telly. It was not built for induction cooktops, ducted heating, a home office and a car on charge. Rewirable fuses protect the wiring. They do nothing to protect the person touching it.

An upgrade swaps those fuses for circuit breakers and RCDs (safety switches) that cut power in about 30 milliseconds when current starts flowing somewhere it shouldn't. We split your circuits sensibly, label everything clearly, and leave room on the board for whatever you add next.

Most upgrades are a same day job. We'll tell you beforehand roughly how long you'll be without power, and we work to keep the fridge and the wifi up as long as we can.

data.heading: What a switchboard upgrade includes.
data.intro: Quoted as one price before we start. Nothing gets added at the end.

items.text: Full inspection of your existing board and main switch
RCD safety switches on every power and lighting circuit
Individual circuit breakers, correctly rated
Neat, clearly labelled circuit directory
Surge protection fitted if you want it
Certificate of Electrical Safety issued on completion
Compliance with AS/NZS 3000 wiring rules
Old board removed and the site left spotless

faqs.question: Do I legally have to upgrade my switchboard?
faqs.answer: There's no law forcing you to replace an existing board that's working. But safety switches are mandatory on new and modified circuits, and most insurers now expect them. If your board still has rewirable fuses, an upgrade is the single biggest safety improvement you can make to the house.

faqs.question: How long does a switchboard upgrade take?
faqs.answer: A typical domestic upgrade takes four to six hours including testing. Larger homes, or boards needing a new main switch and meter work, can run to a full day. You'll have a fixed price and a realistic time frame before we start.

faqs.question: Will I lose power for the whole day?
faqs.answer: No. Power is only off while we transfer circuits across, usually two to three hours. We'll tell you when the outage starts so you can plan around the fridge, the freezer and anyone working from home.

data.title: LED Lighting & Downlights
data.lead: Brighter rooms, lower bills, and no more halogen scorch marks in the ceiling.

data.heading: LED Lighting & Downlights
data.body:
Swapping halogen downlights for LEDs is the quickest win in most homes. A halogen draws about 50 watts and runs hot enough to be a genuine ceiling fire risk. A modern LED gives you the same light, usually better, for around 9 watts, and runs cool.

We'll talk through colour temperature before we start, because it matters more than people expect. Warm white suits bedrooms and living rooms. A cooler neutral white works better in kitchens, laundries and garages. Mixing them room to room is completely normal.

New installs, one for one replacements, dimmable circuits, strip lighting under kitchen cabinetry, feature pendants. All handled, and all cut in neatly so you're not left patching plaster.

data.heading: What an LED install includes.
data.intro: Fittings, install, and the dimmers to match. One price, agreed first.

items.text: Free lighting plan for the rooms you're doing
Warm, neutral or cool white, your call per room
Dimmable options with matched dimmers
Correct clearances and insulation-contact rated fittings
Existing halogen transformers removed, not left in the ceiling
Under-cabinet and feature strip lighting
Tidy cut-outs, no cracked plaster
All fittings covered by manufacturer warranty

faqs.question: How much will LEDs actually save me?
faqs.answer: Replacing twenty 50W halogens with 9W LEDs cuts about 800 watts of draw. Run four hours a night, that's roughly $180–$250 a year off the bill depending on your tariff. You also stop replacing globes every eighteen months.

faqs.question: Can you install downlights in an existing ceiling?
faqs.answer: Yes, in almost every case. We work from the ceiling side wherever possible so there's no need to lift insulation or go into the roof space more than necessary. Double storey homes with limited access sometimes need a slightly different layout, and we'll show you the options first.

faqs.question: Do LED downlights work with my dimmer?
faqs.answer: Not always. Old leading-edge dimmers were built for halogen loads and often flicker or buzz with LEDs. If yours is one of them we'll swap it for a matched trailing-edge dimmer at the same time.

data.title: Powerpoints & Wiring
data.lead: Extra outlets and USB points, so the double adaptors can go in the bin.

data.heading: Powerpoints & Wiring
data.body:
Older homes were wired for a fraction of the appliances we plug in now. If you've got power boards feeding power boards, or you're unplugging the toaster to run the kettle, you don't need another adaptor. You need another circuit.

We add single, double and quad outlets, USB-C and USB-A combination points, weatherproof outdoor outlets, and dedicated circuits for the things that deserve one: ovens, air conditioners, workshop gear and home offices.

Cable gets chased into the wall and made good where we can, and run neatly where we can't. We'll always walk the proposed outlet positions with you before anything gets cut.

data.intro: Cable, outlet, patching and certificate. All inside the quoted price.

items.text: New single, double and quad powerpoints
USB-A and USB-C combination outlets
Weatherproof outdoor and alfresco points
Dedicated circuits for ovens, aircon and workshops
Cable chased into walls and made good
Old or damaged outlets replaced
Circuit tested and added to your board directory
Certificate of Electrical Safety on completion

faqs.question: Can you add a powerpoint to a brick wall?
faqs.answer: Yes. Solid brick and rendered walls take more work than plasterboard so we quote them accordingly, but it's routine. We chase, run the cable, patch, and leave the finish ready for paint.

faqs.question: How many outlets can I run off one circuit?
faqs.answer: The wiring rules don't cap the number outright. What matters is the expected load and the circuit protection. In practice we plan around how the room is actually used, and put high-draw appliances on their own circuit rather than crowding an existing one.

faqs.question: Do I need a licensed electrician just to change a powerpoint?
faqs.answer: Yes. In Victoria any work on fixed wiring, including swapping an outlet, has to be done by a licensed electrician and certified. It's not a DIY job, and doing it yourself can void your insurance.

A ceiling fan is the cheapest cooling in the house, a few cents an hour against dollars for air conditioning. In a well shaded room it's often all you need until the really hot days.

faqs.question: Can you replace my old fan with a new one?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it's usually straightforward. Most swaps take about an hour. If the old fan was mounted straight to the plasterboard we'll add a proper fixing point while we're up there.

faqs.question: Are DC fans worth the extra money?
faqs.answer: For bedrooms, yes. They're noticeably quieter, use around 70% less power, and give you more speed steps. For a rumpus or an alfresco a good AC fan is perfectly fine.

faqs.question: Can I put a ceiling fan in an outdoor area?
faqs.answer: Only an outdoor rated one. Standard indoor fans corrode fast under an alfresco. We'll spec a fan with an IP rating suited to the exposure your area actually gets.

Charging from a standard powerpoint works, but it's slow. Roughly 10 to 15 km of range an hour, so an overnight charge barely covers a decent commute. A dedicated 7kW wall charger does the same job three to four times faster, and stops you tying up a general power circuit for twelve hours a night.

faqs.question: Do I need a switchboard upgrade for an EV charger?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. If your board is full or still on ceramic fuses we'll need to make room and add RCD protection. That gets checked during the free load assessment, so there are no surprises on the day.

faqs.question: How fast will a home charger charge my car?
faqs.answer: A 7kW single-phase charger adds roughly 40 km of range per hour, which is a full overnight charge for almost any EV. Three-phase 11kW or 22kW is faster again, but only if your car can accept it, so it's worth checking before you spend the extra.

faqs.question: Can you install a charger if I park on the street?
faqs.answer: Not safely or legally, because cables can't cross a public footpath. If you have off-street parking anywhere on the property, even a carport at the rear, we can usually run to it.

faqs.question: Should I get an inspection before buying a house?
faqs.answer: It's one of the cheapest pieces of due diligence you can do. A building inspection rarely covers electrical work in any depth. We've found unsafe boards, unpermitted DIY wiring and dead safety switches in homes that passed one.

faqs.question: How often should a home be inspected?
faqs.answer: Every five years for an owner occupied home, or every two years if it's rented or over forty years old. If you've just bought, just renovated, or had recurring trips, get one done now.

faqs.question: What if you find something dangerous?
faqs.answer: Anything immediately unsafe we make safe on the spot and tell you straight away. Everything else goes in the report with a priority and a price, and you decide what gets done and when.

data.heading: Smoke Alarms
data.body:
Smoke alarms expire. Every one has a manufacture date stamped on the back, and after ten years the sensor is no longer reliable, regardless of whether it still chirps when you press the button.

In Victoria, homes built or significantly renovated since August 1997 need mains powered alarms with battery backup. We replace expired units, add alarms where there aren't enough, and interconnect them so that when one sounds they all do. That's what actually gets people out of a house at 3am.

We fit photoelectric alarms as standard. They respond faster to the slow smouldering fires that cause most home fire deaths, and they're far less prone to going off every time you make toast.

data.intro: Alarms, mounting, interconnection, and a dated test on every unit.

faqs.question: How do I know if my smoke alarms have expired?
faqs.answer: Take the alarm off its base. The manufacture date is printed on the back. If it's more than ten years old it needs replacing, even if it still beeps when you test it.

faqs.question: Do my alarms need to be interconnected?
faqs.answer: For new builds and significant renovations, yes. For existing homes it isn't mandatory, but it's the single biggest improvement you can make. An alarm sounding in the laundry doesn't wake anyone in a bedroom at the other end of the house.

faqs.question: What are the rules for rental properties?
faqs.answer: Rental providers must have working alarms installed and tested annually, with records kept. We can handle the annual test and issue documentation you can file.

data.heading: House Rewiring
data.body:
If your house was wired before the late 1960s there's a good chance parts of it still run on rubber or cloth insulated cable. That insulation goes brittle, cracks, and eventually falls away from the conductor, which is how you get arcing inside a wall cavity.

A full rewire replaces every circuit from the board out. We stage it so you're never without power to the kitchen or bathroom for more than a day, and we work around your builder if a renovation is already underway.

This is the moment to think about what you actually want. Where the outlets should be, whether the lighting layout still suits how you use the rooms, data cabling, outdoor circuits. Rewiring twice is expensive.

faqs.question: How long does a full rewire take?
faqs.answer: A three bedroom single storey home is typically five to eight working days, depending on access and whether ceilings and walls are already open. You'll get a staged plan so you know which rooms are affected each day.

faqs.question: Can I stay in the house during a rewire?
faqs.answer: Almost always. We stage the work so the kitchen, bathroom and at least one living area stay live overnight. It's rare for a rewire to need the whole property de-energised for a full day.

faqs.question: Do I have to rewire the whole house at once?
faqs.answer: No. Partial rewires are common, replacing the worst circuits now and the rest later. We'll tell you honestly which parts genuinely need doing and which can safely wait.

data.heading: Fault Finding & Repairs
data.body:
Intermittent faults are the ones that cost people money, because it's tempting to guess. Someone swaps the breaker, the tripping stops for a fortnight, then it's back, and you've paid for a part you never needed.

We isolate faults properly. Split the circuit, test insulation resistance, check earth continuity, and load test until the fault shows itself. Sometimes it's a nail through a cable from a picture hook. Sometimes it's a failing appliance and the wiring is perfectly fine.

You'll be told what the fault actually was, not just that it's fixed. That includes the times the honest answer is that your oven element is on the way out and there's nothing wrong with the circuit.

faqs.question: Why does my safety switch keep tripping?
faqs.answer: Usually a faulty appliance leaking current to earth, moisture in an outdoor circuit, or degraded insulation somewhere in the wiring. It's doing exactly what it's meant to. We find which of the three it is rather than swapping the switch and hoping.

faqs.question: Can you find a fault without opening up my walls?
faqs.answer: In most cases, yes. Testing narrows a fault down to a section of circuit before anything gets opened. If access is unavoidable we'll show you exactly where and why before we cut.

faqs.question: Half my house has no power. Is that an emergency?
faqs.answer: It can be. If you can smell burning, see scorching, or a switch or outlet is hot to touch, turn the main switch off and call us straight away.

faqs.question: Is my hot water problem electrical or plumbing?
faqs.answer: If there's no hot water at all and no leak, it's usually electrical, meaning the element or the thermostat. Leaks, pressure problems and valve failures are plumbing. We'll tell you honestly which one it is rather than charging you for a call-out to say it isn't ours.

faqs.question: Should I switch to off-peak hot water?
faqs.answer: If your system is on continuous supply and your household's usage is fairly predictable, off-peak usually cuts the running cost of the tank by about half. It's a straightforward changeover.

faqs.question: How long does a hot water element last?
faqs.answer: Typically eight to twelve years, less in hard water areas. If your system is over ten years old and the element has already failed once, replacing the whole unit is often better value than another repair.

faqs.question: Will outdoor lighting survive the salt air down here?

faqs.question: Can outdoor lighting run on a timer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Timers, photocells that switch at dusk, or app control. Most people end up with path lighting on dusk to late, and feature lighting on a switch they use when they're outside.

faqs.question: Is low voltage garden lighting better?
faqs.answer: For garden beds and path lighting it's often ideal, and easier to extend later. For floodlighting and alfresco areas mains voltage usually makes more sense. We mix the two where it suits.

faqs.question: Is cabling really better than a mesh wifi system?
faqs.answer: For anything that matters, like video calls, working from home or a media room, yes. Mesh helps, but every hop halves your throughput. Hard-wiring the access points themselves gives you the best of both.

faqs.question: Can you run data cable in an existing house?
faqs.answer: Usually. Single storey homes with roof access are straightforward. Double storey takes more planning and occasionally a small access hole that we make good afterwards. We walk the route with you first.

faqs.question: Can you hide the cables behind my wall mounted TV?
faqs.answer: Yes. We run power and HDMI inside the wall to a recessed outlet behind the screen, so there's nothing visible at all.

data.body:
Plenty of homes down here already have panels on the roof, and the electrical side is often where the problems sit. A board that was never upgraded to suit, an inverter isolator in the wrong place, or export that quietly stopped working months ago.

We prepare switchboards for solar and battery installs, run battery-ready wiring while the walls are already open during a renovation, and diagnose systems that aren't producing what they should.

We're not chasing solar sales. If your system is fine and the problem is your retailer's tariff, we'll tell you that.

faqs.question: My solar production has dropped. What's wrong?
faqs.answer: Most commonly a tripped or failed isolator, a string fault, or an inverter that's been sitting in an error state for weeks without anyone noticing. All are testable. Shading from a grown tree accounts for a surprising number too.

faqs.question: Should I wire for a battery now even if I'm not buying one yet?
faqs.answer: If your walls are open for a renovation, absolutely. The cabling is cheap while everything's accessible and expensive once it's plastered, and it doesn't commit you to anything.

faqs.question: Do you sell and install solar panels?
faqs.answer: We don't sell systems. We do the electrical work around them, so our advice on your existing setup comes with nothing attached.

faqs.question: Do you work outside business hours?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most fitout and maintenance work we prefer to. It usually costs less overall than closing for a day.

faqs.question: How often does emergency lighting need testing?
faqs.answer: Every six months, with a 90 minute discharge test annually, and records kept. We can put you on a schedule so it's handled without you having to track it.

faqs.question: Can you handle test and tag for our office?
faqs.answer: Yes, including a documented register of every item, its test date and next due date. That's the thing auditors actually ask for.
